usefulness.example: An introductory C course with 450 students submits weekly lab assignments. The agent grades every upload in under 3 seconds with identical strictness on correctness, compiler hygiene, modularity, and ASan memory safety.
usefulness.benefit: Eliminates grading variance across TAs and gives students immediate counterexamples.

usefulness.use_case: Coding-interview and embedded systems hiring screens
usefulness.example: A company runs 500 candidate submissions for an 'add two integers safely' task. The agent ranks them by correctness, edge-case handling and memory safety, and gives an explainable per-metric score.
usefulness.benefit: Fast first-round filtering where every rejection can be justified metric by metric.

usefulness.use_case: Plagiarism and LLM-copy triage for instructors
usefulness.example: Two submissions reach a similarity of 0.93 against the 0.85 threshold, so the agent raises a flag in the report. The instructor reviews only those pairs instead of all 300.
usefulness.benefit: Saves review time by narrowing manual checking to suspicious cases.

usefulness.use_case: Continuous self-check pre-submission hook for students
usefulness.example: Students run c-autograder locally before pushing to Git; the sanitizer_run and edge_case_runner analyzers catch signed 32-bit overflow and off-by-one bugs early.
usefulness.benefit: Teaches defensive C programming habits through concrete failing inputs.

limitations.limitation: Finite I/O tests cannot prove mathematical correctness
limitations.example: A submission passes all 10 hidden tests but fails when the input has extra whitespace or a trailing newline that no test covers, or hardcodes a lookup table for small inputs. The agent still reports 10/10 on correctness.
limitations.mitigation: Combine fixed regression tests with property-based randomized fuzzing against a reference oracle binary.

limitations.limitation: Empirical timing curves can misclassify complexity on noisy hosts
limitations.example: An O(n) loop with a tiny constant factor finishes in 0.4ms for n=1..100 while OS scheduling jitter adds 0.8ms of variance, causing complexity_estimator to label an O(n) algorithm as O(1) (or vice versa).
limitations.mitigation: Combine AST loop-bound static analysis with hardware instruction counters (perf) rather than wall-clock time alone.

limitations.limitation: Token-shingle similarity can false-positive on short boilerplate problems
limitations.example: For a 10-line 'add two integers' task, two independent students who write standard scanf/printf with a helper function can exceed 0.85 token cosine similarity despite zero collusion.
limitations.mitigation: Discount template boilerplate tokens and require a minimum AST node count before raising a similarity flag.

limitations.limitation: Heuristic / LLM readability rubrics can be gamed with superficial comments
limitations.example: A student adds meaningless comments ('// function') and long meaningless variable names ('variable_one_number') over spaghetti logic, receiving 10/10 on readability.
limitations.mitigation: Cross-check comment semantic relevance against AST operations and enforce human TA spot checks on borderline style scores.
